newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate pares rise, election fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate pares rise, election fears ease.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates trimmed their earlier increase to close up a marginal 5 basis points at 20.65 percent on Friday.
Dealers said early jitters over this weekend's mid-term elections ebbed away in late trade, dealers.
"Elections are no longer hurting the market, and demand for paper could increase on Monday when U.S. investors return to the market," a trader said.
U.S. financial markets closed on Friday for the July 4 Independence Day holiday.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.

The outcome of the mayoral race is critical, because for the first time President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may lose control of the nerve center of Mexico to an opposition party. The PRI has ruled Mexico for 68 unbroken years.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile fell 90 basis points to 20.75 percent.
Banco de Mexico drained 9.019 billion pesos from the market through three direct sales of paper and 11 repos.
Liquidity of 1.340 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
